AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MARCH 1, 2022
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE
GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDER N-15-21, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE
FROM A REMOTE LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS
DURING A MEETING: YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO:
publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING
THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709
573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER
CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Rick Ramirez, Mayor
  Ana Valencia, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING - 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT
  CODE §54956.9(d)(1) City of Norwalk vs. Regional Water Quality Control Board, Case No.
  21STCP04148.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED  LITIGATION  PURSUANT  TO
  GOVERNMENT CODE §54956.9(d)(4) in one case.

RECESS

REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

INVOCATION
  Divvy Cowgila and Kishan Hingorani
  Sindhu Center

FLAG SALUTE
  Liba Malik, 8th grade
  Lake Center Middle School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS
  City Council to recognize February as Social Services Worker month in the City of Norwalk.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Athens Disposal regarding Assembly Bill 1383 and its Impacts on the Community.

  3.  Public Safety Sergeant

  4.  Department Highlights – City Clerk.

  5.  Week in Review.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.
 1.  MEETING MINUTES - Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of
  February 15, 2022. 825-04

  Report

2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period January 23, 2022 –
  February 5, 2022, in the total amount of $983,450.36. 630

  Report

3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  February 10, 2022 - February 24, 2022 in the total amount of $2,369,089.86. 640

  Report

4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Amy Cook,
  Michael Hash, and Jeanette Vidal. 830-03/08/22

  Report

5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – FEBRUARY 23, 2022 - Staff recommends that City Council
  receive and file the 2021 General Plan and Housing Element Annual Progress Report and direct staff
  to transmit the report to the Governor’s Office of Planning and Research and the Department of
  Housing and Community Development. 320

  Report

6.  RESOLUTION NO. 22-16 – DESTRUCTION OF OBSOLETE RECORDS – CITY CLERK AND SOCIAL
  SERVICES DEPARTMENTS - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-16, A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE
  DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN RECORDS IN THE CITY CLERK AND SOCIAL SERVICES
  DEPARTMENTS. 870-02

  Report

7.  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION APPROVAL OF BLUE CURB AT 11872 HERMOSURA STREET - No
  action is required unless the City Council elects to review the decision of the Public Safety Commission
  regarding approval of the blue curb.

  Report

8.  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION APPROVAL OF BLUE CURB AT 11519 ALONDRA BOULEVARD -
  No action is required unless the City Council elects to review the decision of the Public Safety
  Commission regarding approval of the blue curb.

  Report

9.  FEDERAL TRANSIT ADMINISTRATION CERTIFICATIONS AND ASSURANCES FOR FEDERAL
  FISCAL YEAR 2022 – Staff recommends City Council authorize the Executive Director of Regional
  Transportation to execute the Fiscal Year 2022 Certifications and Assurances Federal Transit
  Administration Assistance Programs/Affirmation of Applicant, file grant application(s) on behalf of the
  City and execute a grant agreement(s); in concurrence with and execution of the Affirmation of
  Applicant’s Attorney Certification by the City Attorney.

  Report

10. PROJECT NO. 7924.2 - ACCEPTANCE OF WORK - LOCAL STREET REHABILITATION PROGRAM
  PAVING IMPROVEMENTS IN ZONE 24, ENGINEERS REPORT NO. 22-05 – Staff recommends City
  Council accept the work of R.J. Noble Company, in the amount of $1,442,105.31, for Project No.
  7924.2 - Local Street Rehabilitation Program paving improvements. 1005-04-7924

  Report

11. PROJECT NO. 7925.2 - ACCEPTANCE OF WORK - LOCAL STREET REHABILITATION PROGRAM
   PAVING IMPROVEMENTS IN ZONE 27, ENGINEERS REPORT NO. 22-03 - Staff recommends City
  Council accept the work of R.J. Noble Company, in the amount of $594,176.25 for Project No. 7925.2 -
  Local Street Rehabilitation Program, paving improvements. 1005-04-7925

  Report

  12. PROJECT NO. 7926.2 - RESOLUTION NO. 22-15 - BUDGET AMENDMENT AND ACCEPTANCE OF
  WORK - LOCAL STREET REHABILITATION PROGRAM PAVING IMPROVEMENTS IN ZONE 32 -
  ENGINEERS REPORT NO. 22-04 - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 22-15, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE ROAD MAINTENANCE AND REHABILITATION ACCOUNT FUNDS
  FOR PROJECT NO. 7926.2 – LOCAL STREETS REHABILITATION PROGRAM PAVING
  IMPROVEMENTS – ZONE 32, in the amount of $490,683; and

  b.  accept the work of R.J. Noble Company, in the amount of $1,051,102.27, for Project No. 7926.2,
  Local Street Rehabilitation Program paving improvements. 1005-04-7926

  Report

  13. AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 7 - EXCLUSIVE NEGOTIATION AGREEMENT FOR THE
  DEVELOPMENT OF THE CIVIC CENTER - Staff recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 7
  with Primestor; refining the terms and conditions of the agreement and extending the agreement
  through June 30, 2023, and authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment and any additional
  amendments provided there is funding in the budget, in a form authorized by the City Attorney.

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  14. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

PUBLIC HEARINGS

  15. APPEAL OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION’S REVOCATION OF NONCONFORMING ALCOHOL
  SALES USE - YOUNG JAE KWAK, MIKE’S LIQUOR, 14408 PIONEER BOULEVARD - Staff
  recommends City Council uphold the Planning Commission’s decision to terminate and revoke the
  nonconforming use of the Subject Property for the sale of alcoholic beverages.

  Report

REPORTS

  16. NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 8.56 - FORECLOSURE, BOARDING-UP, & SCREENING
  UPDATE - Staff recommends City Council consider the information and provide direction on the
  proposed amendments.

  Report

  17. PROPOSED ACTIVITIES FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022/23 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN FOR THE
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT AND HOME INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIPS
  PROGRAM - Staff is seeking input from City Council regarding proposed activities for the Fiscal Year
  2022/23 Annual Action Plan prior to the public hearing scheduled for March 15, 2022. 315

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT
 I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated February 25, 2022.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
